## Before you start {.study}

- **What you need:** your university account, and a computer or a phone with
  a browser. On a phone, the free OneDrive and Word apps also work.
- **Time:** about 60 minutes. Work alone, at your own speed.
- **How it works:** do Steps 1–3 on this page. Each step has a short text, a
  simulator to try and a self-check with instant feedback. Then do the
  **Tasks to submit** at the end.
- **What you submit:** one screenshot and your answers to Tasks 2–4, on the
  university e-learning platform, before lecture 3.

## Key terms {.study}

{{< glossary account authentication single-sign-on file folder file-path file-extension cloud-storage synchronization backup >}}

## Step 1 · One account, one sign-in {.study}

- Your **account**: your user name, your password and your data.
- **Authentication**: you prove that the account is yours. Something you
  **know** (a password), **have** (your phone) or **are** (your fingerprint).
- **Single sign-on (SSO)**: you sign in one time, and all university
  services open: e-mail, the e-learning platform, Microsoft 365, OneDrive.
- Risk: a stolen password opens everything.
- On a shared or lab computer: press **Sign out**, never save your password,
  and lock the screen when you leave (Windows key + L).

![Single sign-on: one sign-in, many services.](images/sso.png){width=84%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Closing the browser does not always sign you out. Press **Sign out** first.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Accounts and sign-in"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="something you are"}
A code comes to your phone. Which kind of proof is it?
:   something you have

Your password. Which kind of proof is it?
:   something you know

You sign in one time, and e-mail and OneDrive both open. What is this called?
:   single sign-on

What is the risk of single sign-on?
:   a stolen password opens everything

You leave a lab computer for one minute. What do you do?
:   lock the screen
:::
:::

## Step 2 · Folders, paths and good file names {.study}

- A **file** is one saved piece of work. A **folder** keeps files and other
  folders. Folders in folders make a tree.
- The **path** is the full address of a file, for example
  `C:\Users\Sara\Documents\Courses\Digital-Skills\lecture-02\cv.docx`.
  Two files can have the same name, but never the same path.
- The **extension** shows the type: `.docx` Word, `.xlsx` Excel, `.pptx`
  PowerPoint, `.jpg` a photo, `.exe` a program.
- Four rules for good file names:
  1. say what it is (`cv`, not `New Document`);
  2. no spaces: use `-` or `_`;
  3. the date as year-month-day (2026-10-26), so files sort by date;
  4. versions `v01`, `v02`, never `final`, `final2`.

![A folder tree for your courses.](images/folder-tree.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/path-finder.html" poster="sims/path-finder.png" title="Path Finder: files, folders and paths" kind="game" height="600" >}}

{{< sim file="sims/folder-lab.html" poster="sims/folder-lab.png" title="Folder Lab: folders and good file names" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
`invoice.pdf.exe` looks like `invoice.pdf` when Windows hides extensions. It
is a program. In File Explorer, turn on **View → Show → File name
extensions**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Paths and names"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="21-10-2026|final_v2_new"}
Two files are both called `cv.docx`. What is always different?
:   their paths

Which app opens `budget.xlsx`?
:   Excel

A file is called `photo.jpg.exe`. What is it really?
:   a program

Which date format sorts files by date?
:   2026-10-26

A better name for `final final.pptx` (an English talk, 12 November 2026, third version)?
:   2026-11-12_english-talk_v03.pptx
:::
:::

## Step 3 · Cloud storage, sync and backup {.study}

- **Cloud storage** (OneDrive, Google Drive) keeps your files on the
  Internet. You open them on any device after you sign in.
- **Sync** keeps the same files on all your devices. It also copies your
  mistakes: delete a file in one place, and it is gone everywhere.
- The **recycle bin** of the cloud keeps deleted files for some days.
- A **backup** is an extra copy in a separate place, for example a USB
  stick. A mistake does not reach it.
- **3-2-1 rule:** 3 copies, on 2 kinds of storage, 1 copy in another place.

![Sync copies every change; a backup is a separate copy.](images/sync-backup.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/sync-lab.html" poster="sims/sync-lab.png" title="Sync Lab: sync, recycle bin and backup" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Sync or backup?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="sync is a backup|2 copies"}
You delete a file on the lab computer. What happens on your synced phone?
:   it is deleted too

A copy of your work on a USB stick at home. What is it?
:   a backup

Where can you find a deleted cloud file for some days?
:   the recycle bin

The 3-2-1 rule: how many copies?
:   3 copies
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

### Task 1 · Your course folders (2 marks)

1. In OneDrive (browser or app), make `Courses` → `Digital-Skills` → `lecture-02`.
2. Make a Word document with your name and today's date. Save it in
   `lecture-02` with a good name, for example `2026-10-26_first-file_v01.docx`.
3. Take a screenshot that shows the path and the file. *Submit:* the screenshot.

### Task 2 · Better file names (2 marks)

Write a better name for each file.

a) `Document1 (2).docx`: your English homework, 3 November 2026, first version.

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) `talk FINAL final.pptx`: your Arabic talk, 10 November 2026, second version.

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

c) `IMG_5530.jpg`: a photo of the class trip, 31 October 2026.

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

### Task 3 · A path (1 mark)

User **Omar** has `notes.docx` on a Windows computer, in the folder
`lecture-02`, in `Digital-Skills`, in `Courses`, in `Documents`. Write its
path (its full address).

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

### Task 4 · Sync or backup? (1 mark)

Lina's folder is synced on her laptop and her phone. Every Friday she copies
it to a USB stick. On Monday she deletes `report.docx` on her laptop by
mistake.

a) Is `report.docx` still on her phone? Why?

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) Where can she get it back first? Where is her backup?

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}
